title: Usage statistics — the questions before anything is drawn

steps.path: Wherever you would go to see how much you have used
steps.headline: Where should a full picture of your usage live?
steps.today: Usage is scattered: status-bar chips for the current chat, a /usage card you type for, and plan limit bars inside Settings → Cloud providers. Each shows one chat or one moment.
steps.problem: There is no single place to see what you used today, this week, or which model or chat ate your ChatGPT plan or OpenRouter credit.
steps.proposal: Add one home for usage. Pick where you would actually look for it.

options.label: New Usage page
options.summary: Its own page in Settings, next to Cloud providers, with limit bars, balances and history together.
pros: Room for history, charts and every provider at once.
The limit bars and balances already live nearby in Settings, so everything about accounts stays together.
cons: Two clicks away while you are chatting.
One more Settings page.

options.label: Status-bar popup
options.summary: Clicking a usage chip in the status bar opens a larger panel.
pros: One click from any chat.
No new page to learn.
cons: A popup is small, so history and per-model breakdowns get cramped.
Only reachable if you have a usage chip turned on.

options.label: Both
options.summary: A small summary in the status-bar popup, with a button to the full Usage page.
pros: Quick glance while chatting, full detail when you want it.
cons: Two surfaces to keep consistent, so this is more work to build and keep working.

steps.headline: Which breakdowns do you want to see?
steps.today: The app records how much each reply used and cost in the app's own chats, but never adds them up past one chat.
steps.problem: Without breakdowns you cannot tell whether one long chat, one expensive model, or the helpers used up your allowance. In the last 3 days, helpers were 59% of your ChatGPT usage and nothing in the app shows that.
steps.proposal: Pick every breakdown you would use. Fewer means a simpler page.

options.label: By day
pros: Shows when usage spikes, and whether a day's work was unusual.
cons: Adds a chart.

options.label: By provider
pros: ChatGPT plan vs OpenRouter vs Claude side by side.
cons: None worth noting.

options.label: By model
pros: Shows whether a pricier model is the cause.
cons: Model names change often, so the list can get long.

options.label: By chat
pros: Finds the one runaway conversation.
Could link straight to it.
cons: A long list once you have many chats.

options.label: Helpers vs main chat
pros: Answers the exact question from today: helpers were the biggest chunk.
cons: Another split to read.

steps.headline: Should Claude Code sessions be counted in the same view?
steps.today: Claude Code keeps its own records on your computer, and the app shows only its plan limit bars and the current session's cost.
steps.problem: If only the app's own chats are counted, the page tells half the story for someone like you who uses both.
steps.proposal: Yes: read Claude Code's records too and show them as their own provider. No: this view covers only the app's own chats; Claude Code keeps its limit bars.

options.label: Include it
pros: One place for everything you use.
Makes comparisons like today's (Claude Code sent 5x more) visible.
cons: Its dollar figure is what the work would cost at pay-per-use prices, not what your subscription charges, which could alarm you if read wrong.
Reading Claude Code's records adds some startup work.

options.label: App chats only
pros: Simpler, and every number is from the app itself.
cons: Can't compare the two side by side.

steps.path: The new usage view, for ChatGPT and Claude plans
steps.headline: For monthly plans, what should the numbers say?
steps.today: Plans like ChatGPT and Claude show percentage bars for their 5-hour and 7-day limits. Neither company says exactly how a reply counts against them.
steps.problem: A raw count of words processed means nothing to most people, and a dollar figure for a plan you already paid for can mislead.
steps.proposal: Pick how plan usage is described.

options.label: Limit bars plus shares
options.summary: Keep the limit bars, and show each chat's or model's share of the usage as a percentage.
pros: Answers 'what ate my limit' without inventing a price.
Nothing that looks like a bill.
cons: No way to compare with OpenRouter in dollars.

options.label: Dollar equivalent
options.summary: Show what the same work would cost at pay-per-use prices, clearly labelled as an estimate.
pros: One unit (dollars) across every provider.
cons: It is an estimate, and can look like a charge you owe.

options.label: Both
pros: The most information.
cons: Busier page; the dollar figure still needs a careful label.

steps.intro: The first page decided what the history shows. These decide what live account info appears, and whether the app warns you.

steps.path: Settings → Cloud providers → OpenRouter, and the usage view
steps.headline: Should the app show your remaining OpenRouter credit?
steps.today: The OpenRouter row only says whether your key works. To see your balance you go to OpenRouter's website. This was already designed in August but never built.
steps.problem: You find out credit is gone when a reply fails.
steps.proposal: Yes: show the balance (refreshed every few minutes and after each reply) on the OpenRouter row and the usage view, built to the August design. No: keep linking to the website.

options.label: Show balance
pros: You see credit running down before it runs out.
Already designed, so it's quicker to build.
cons: A light extra check with OpenRouter every few minutes while the app is open.

options.label: Keep the link
pros: Nothing changes.
cons: Surprise failures stay possible.

steps.path: Settings → Cloud providers → ChatGPT, and the usage view
steps.headline: Should the ChatGPT row also show extra credits and per-model limits ChatGPT already sends?
steps.today: ChatGPT sends more than the app shows: an extra-credits balance and usage per model. The app reads only the 5-hour and 7-day bars.
steps.problem: If your plan includes extra credits or a separate limit for one model, the app hides it, so a stop can look unexplained.
steps.proposal: Yes: show them when ChatGPT provides them and hide them when it doesn't. No: bars only.

options.label: Show them
pros: Explains stops the bars alone don't.
No extra requests: the data already arrives.
cons: Depends on details ChatGPT doesn't document, so a line may disappear if they change it.

options.label: Bars only
pros: Simpler row.
cons: Hidden limits stay hidden.

steps.path: Anywhere in the app while you work
steps.headline: Should the app warn you before a plan limit or credit balance runs out?
steps.today: Nothing warns you. The first sign is a failed reply or a limit message.
steps.problem: A long task can stop halfway, and you only learn why afterwards.
steps.proposal: Pick how loud a warning should be.

options.label: No warnings
pros: Nothing interrupts you.
cons: Surprise stops continue.

options.label: Quiet colour change
options.summary: The usage chip and the Settings gear turn amber at 80% and red at 95%.
pros: Visible without interrupting.
Matches the red dot already planned for OpenRouter.
cons: Easy to miss if the chip is turned off.

options.label: One notice at 80%
options.summary: A single message in the chat when you cross 80%, plus the colour change.
pros: Hard to miss.
cons: Interrupts; could feel naggy for people near their limit often.

steps.headline: How far back should usage history go?
steps.today: The app keeps no usage history beyond each chat's own record. Nothing leaves your computer.
steps.problem: Without history you can't compare this week with last week, or tell whether a change helped.
steps.proposal: Pick how long to keep daily totals. They stay on your computer either way.

options.label: 90 days
pros: Covers a full plan cycle plus comparisons.
Tiny on disk.
cons: Older history is gone.

options.label: Forever
pros: Full history.
cons: Grows slowly without end; not useful to most people.

options.label: 30 days
pros: Smallest.
cons: Too short to compare months.

steps.headline: On Android, this first version shows Claude Code usage only.
steps.changed: Stated, not asked: Android can't run the app's own assistant yet, so it has no ChatGPT or OpenRouter chats to count. Android picks up the rest when that arrives.
steps.notice: The usage view on your phone lists Claude Code only, with a line saying the rest comes later.
